Issue_Name: Addressables build contains duplicated implicit dependencies
Recommended_Fix_Mode: Diagnostic until a concrete safe action/verifier exists
Current_Implementation_Status: Implemented in analyzer: exposes group packing-mode ReviewFix alternatives for configured Addressables groups. User must correlate the duplicate BuildLayout result to the intended group; Unity integration not run.
Current_Postcondition_Verification: Each option has a BundleMode postcondition verifier for its specific Addressables group. Group asset path must be under Assets; action requires backup, Undo, dirty/save, and fails closed when the schema or group cannot be resolved. Not runtime-tested.
Current_Implementation_Concern: Packing mode mutates the whole group, not just duplicate records. The duplicate result lacks a stable correlation key to the exact group, so options are deliberately not preselected; no options may be emitted when the settings/schema cannot be resolved.
Rule_Specific_Claim_To_Prove: The official Addressables BuildLayout identifies objects/assets that were implicitly included more than once. Duplication inflates content delivery and can create unnecessary bundle residency/download cost.
Required_Severity_Gate: Confirm active Build Profile/platform and freshness/provenance of build or settings evidence before changing project-wide configuration.
Verification_and_Safety: Keep the issue informational and aggregated. Do not present a “Review” label as if an executable action exists; define the normal-case policy, machine-detect exceptions and add a deterministic verifier before adding a fix. Require a fresh Addressables Analyze/BuildLayout report whose Unity/package version, target and build context match; actual runtime loading boundaries determine appropriate group topology.
Decision_Rationale: Keep as Review: duplicate implicit dependencies are real build-layout evidence, but a global regrouping is not universally safe. Unity documents cases where the built-in duplicate-bundle fixer can be harmful (for example, multi-object FBX sub-assets used by different groups or content split by audience/region). Human choice about co-loading, memory residency, and download boundaries remains irreducible.
Common_Case_Automation_Possible: Partially. Candidate duplicates and cost can be computed; automatically changing topology is only safe when a machine-verifiable loading-lifetime policy exists. No such policy is present in this snapshot.
Machine_Detectable_Exceptions: Stale or mismatched BuildLayout; missing group/asset identity; sub-assets; region/platform variants; independent load lifetimes; remote catalogs; custom build scripts; any overlap with ADR007 without stable shared evidence identity.
Required_Action_or_Code_Changes: Add a ReviewFix preview listing exact duplicated asset/sub-asset, source bundles/groups, expected bundle changes and potential blast radius. Offer the Addressables Analyze built-in fix only when its rule reports CanFix, after explicit user selection; do not auto-apply. Keep ADR001 distinct from ADR007.
Required_Evidence_and_Preflight: Require complete BuildLayout provenance (Unity/package version, active profile, target, build context), exact asset/sub-asset identifiers, current Addressables settings and source group membership. Reject stale reports and missing keys.
Required_Verifier_and_Rollback: Rebuild content and compare duplicate dependency records, bundle membership/size and load dependencies. Preserve original settings/assets and an operation-specific backup; restore on failed build, changed unrelated groups or incomplete verification.
Regression_Test_Plan: Test safe duplicate candidate preview; multi-object FBX; independent load-lifetime groups; platform/region split; stale BuildLayout rejection; wrong-target rejection; build output matches preview; cancelled operation no mutation; failed verifier triggers rollback; ADR001 and ADR007 remain separately visible.
Audit_Status: ReviewFix implemented within analyzer; static validation only; Unity/EditMode and real asset/player-build validation not run

Rule_Specific_Claim_To_Prove: BuildLayout measures how much of a dependency bundle is actually used by its parent. A very small efficiency ratio can mean a large shared bundle is being pulled in for a small dependency, increasing download and load overhead.

Common_Case_Automation_Possible: Partially. Ratios and candidate splits are computable, but source data does not establish intended runtime load/unload boundaries.

Unity’s current documentation notes performance costs especially above four influences and confirms that reducing `maxBonesPerVertex` discards the lowest-weight influences. Four is a reasonable general default; two would be unnecessarily aggressive as a broad default. The current action is buggy because `Mathf.Clamp(2, 1, 255)` always sets 2 regardless of the advertised “4 or fewer” recommendation.

Do not require per-asset animated-pose comparison as a prerequisite under the user’s policy; the user can raise the limit on exceptional assets whose deformation is unacceptable.

These exceptions are technical applicability/failure conditions, not subjective deformation exceptions.
Required_Action_or_Code_Changes: Promote to Verified and replace the hard-coded `Mathf.Clamp(2, 1, 255)` with the explicit target `4`. Fix the display text so it states the action actually taken, remove Review-only warning, preserve prior importer settings for failed-operation rollback, and verify the imported mesh stores no more than four influences per vertex after reimport.
Required_Evidence_and_Preflight: Fresh source/import fingerprint; skinned mesh exists; ModelImporter skinWeights mode is Custom; maxBonesPerVertex > 4; importer is writable; record old maximum and skin-weight/import settings.
